run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T23:00:27Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend is explained by frontend HTTP 500s from failed gRPC calls to two dependencies whose Service ClusterIPs refused TCP connections between roughly 23:00 and 23:07 (ad) and 23:00-23:02 (payment). The error text is explicit: frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans failed with '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080', and checkout PlaceOrder failed with '13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card ... dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused'; those two IPs are the ad and payment Service ClusterIPs. Both deployments had been restarted at 22:58:53Z (pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt, ReplicaSet replacement, old pods killed at 22:58:56/57) without any image change. The replacement ad and payment containers define no readiness probe and were marked Ready within 1-2 s of container start, while their CPU usage sat exactly at their very small limits (ad 50m, payment 20m) with CFS throttling of 92-100 percent of periods for the whole ad outage window; throttling fell away at 23:07-23:09 as ad resumed serving. Hypothesis: the restarted, CPU-throttled pods could not serve, and because they were published as Ready immediately, callers got connection refused instead of waiting, which surfaced as frontend 500s. What triggered the 22:58:53 rollout is unknown because change history is not integrated; the flagd fault flags adFailure=on and paymentFailure=100 percent do not match the observed transport-level refusals. No pod crash, OOM, eviction or node pressure was observed.

claims.text: Frontend recorded error spans on its own HTTP and client operations during the window: GET, GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds share one identical error-rate curve (0 until 23:00:27Z, peak 0.8667 per second at 23:04:27Z, 0 again at 23:11:27Z), and a separate curve covers POST, POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder. All carry status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR; the corresponding GET and POST client spans carry http.status_code 500.

Per-minute span increases show the ad path failing completely: frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds ERROR spans were 24 in the minute ending 23:00:00Z, 140 at 23:01, 110 at 23:02, 110 at 23:05, 76 at 23:06, 84 at 23:07 and 0 at 23:08, while non-error (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) GetAds spans were 100-130 per minute before 23:00 and 110 and 148 again at 23:08 and 23:09; there were no non-error GetAds spans at all during 23:01-23:07.

The ad service own server spans mirror this: oteldemo.AdService/GetAds had 74 spans in the minute ending 23:00:00Z and 0 in the minutes ending 23:01, 23:02, 23:05, 23:06 and 23:07 (samples absent for 23:03 and 23:04), then 144 at 23:09. Over 22:56:33-23:16:33 the ad service recorded 0 error spans of its own.

The exact error text on frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans is '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080', with rpc.grpc.status_code 14 and otel.status_code ERROR, propagating up through executing api route (pages) /api/data, GET /api/data and GET with http.status_code 500.

100.65.180.246 is the ad Service ClusterIP (ClusterIP, port 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad) and 100.70.188.60 is the payment Service ClusterIP (ClusterIP, port 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment), so the refusals were against the Services, not against a named pod IP.

The checkout path failed with the exact text '13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card: could not charge the card: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused' on the frontend grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans (rpc.grpc.status_code 13) and on executing api route (pages) /api/checkout.

The checkout service recorded its own errors: oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and its client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge had error increases of 59.77 in the minute ending 23:01:00Z and 4 at 23:02 and 0 afterwards, while the payment service itself recorded 0 error spans in the whole window and its oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge server spans were 46 at 23:00, 0 at 23:01 and 23:02, and 60 again at 23:05.

Both deployments were rolled at 22:58:53Z: Deployment ad scaled up replicaset ad-6cb57f76d from 0 to 1 and scaled ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0, Deployment payment scaled up payment-9c8ffb665 from 0 to 1 and scaled payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0; pods ad-554b849958-mbnxm and payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb were Killing at 22:58:56Z and 22:58:57Z, and new pods ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 were scheduled at 22:58:53Z with containers started at 22:58:55Z and 22:58:56Z.

The deployment objects ad and payment carry deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2 and a pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T22:58:53Z; their containers define no readinessProbe and no livenessProbe, and resource limits cpu 50m and memory 450Mi (ad), cpu 20m and memory 160Mi (payment).

The old and new ReplicaSets for both workloads use the same images and identical pod templates apart from the restartedAt annotation: ad-554b849958 and ad-6cb57f76d both use ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, payment-55766d76b9 and payment-9c8ffb665 both use ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, and only the new ReplicaSet templates carry kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt.

The replacement pods reached Ready 1-2 s after container start: ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 has Ready and ContainersReady True with lastTransitionTime 2026-11-16T22:58:56Z (container running since 22:58:55Z, restartCount 0, lastState empty) and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 has Ready True at 22:58:57Z (container running since 22:58:56Z, restartCount 0); both are owned by their ReplicaSets, which are owned by Deployments ad and payment.

The replacement containers were throttled at their CPU limits exactly during the outage: ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 used 0.047-0.0496 cores against its 0.05-core limit with a throttled-period ratio of 0.924 in the minute ending 23:00:00Z, 0.986 at 23:01, 1.0 at 23:02 through 23:06, 0.838 at 23:07, 0.363 at 23:08 and 0.189 at 23:09, whereas the previous pod ad-554b849958-mbnxm ran at 0.0028-0.0058 cores with ratio 0.009-0.167; payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 used 0.02 cores against its 0.02-core limit with ratio 1.0 at 23:00, 0.928 at 23:01, 0.753 at 23:02 and 0.22-0.44 afterwards, versus 0.0054-0.0073 cores and ratio 0.10-0.23 for payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb.

No pod-damage or node-level marks were found: all five nodes report Ready True with MemoryPressure False and DiskPressure False (node i-0e9f8b08cc290a884, which hosts the new ad and payment pods, Ready since 2026-11-13T01:10:21Z, allocatable 4 CPU and 16064768Ki), and there are no Evicted, OOMKilling or NodeNotReady events; the only FailedScheduling events are Pod jaeger-traces-recorder-0 at 22:43:32Z and Pod prometheus-alert-recorder-0 at 22:42:30Z in namespace data-recorders, failing on a VolumeBinding PVC conflict before the error onset.

Current state is recovered: all 21 otel-demo pods are Running with ready true and restartCount 0, including ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84; ad logs (retained fragment 23:06:49-23:08:19Z) show 'no baggage found in context' and 'Targeted ad request received for [...]' with no error lines, and payment logs (fragment 23:05:33-23:08:22Z) show repeated pairs of 'Charge request received.' and 'Transaction complete.'.

The scope of recorded error spans over 22:56:33-23:16:33Z is frontend 1759.15, frontend-proxy 885.24, checkout 69.67, recommendation 2.06, fraud-detection 2.06, and 0 for ad, payment, cart and accounting; the two roughly 2-span counts are too small to tie to this failure on the evidence available.

The flagd-config ConfigMap declares fault-injection flags with adFailure defaultVariant on (Fail ad service), paymentFailure defaultVariant 100 percent (Fail payment service charge requests n percent), and adHighCpu, adManualGc, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure all off.

The fault originates in Deployment ad: its pod template was rolled at 22:58:53Z (pod-template restartedAt annotation, ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 replaced by ad-6cb57f76d), the replacement container saturated its 50m CPU limit with 92-100 percent CFS throttling for about seven minutes, and during that period connections to the ad Service ClusterIP 100.65.180.246:8080 were refused, which produced frontend GET /api/data 500s and the RequestErrorRate alert. This is a hypothesis because the evidence cannot show the internal state of the new process, and why it burned CPU at its limit is not observable.

A second, parallel fault originated in Deployment payment: its pod template was rolled at the same instant (payment-55766d76b9 replaced by payment-9c8ffb665), the replacement container ran at its 20m CPU limit with throttling 1.0, 0.928 and 0.753 in the minutes ending 23:00-23:02, and connections to the payment Service ClusterIP 100.70.188.60:8080 were refused, producing checkout PlaceOrder errors (59.77 and 4 error spans in the minutes ending 23:01 and 23:02) and frontend POST /api/checkout 500s.

Because neither container defines a readiness probe, the replacement pods were declared Ready (ad 22:58:56Z, payment 22:58:57Z) and therefore eligible as Service endpoints about 1-2 s after container start, before the applications were accepting connections; callers were therefore routed to not-yet-listening pods and received connection refused instead of being held until the backends were ready. The Ready timestamps and the missing probes are observed; the endpoint consequence is inferred.

The flagd fault settings do not match the observed failure path: the errors are TCP-level connect connection refused against the ad and payment Service ClusterIPs, the ad and payment services recorded no error spans of their own (0 over the window) and their server-side operations received no requests at all during the burst, and the ad path was serving normally again at 23:08-23:09 while the ConfigMap still declares adFailure on; an application-level flag-declared failure would not produce connection refusals.

Rejected: pod crash, OOM, eviction or node resource pressure as the cause. Both replacement pods have restartCount 0 and empty lastState, there are no OOMKilling, Evicted or NodeNotReady events in the window, and all nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure False and DiskPressure False.

Rejected: the frontend pod itself is the origin. It has been running since 2026-11-16T22:25:10Z/22:25:11Z with restartCount 0 and no restart event, its pod was not part of the 22:58:53Z rollout (only ad and payment ReplicaSets were created and deleted), and its error spans carry the downstream connection-refused diagnostics.

Rejected: the 22:58:56Z and 22:58:57Z termination of the old pods is itself the damage. The old pods were deleted by their own controller (ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete plus Deployment ScalingReplicaSet 1 to 0 at the same moment as the new ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate) with new pod names and restartCount 0, i.e. the rollout mechanism; the lasting errors come from the replacement pods being unreachable, not from the deletion event.

Add a gRPC readiness probe to the ad and payment containers so that Service endpoints only include pods that are actually listening; today a 1-2 s container start makes them Ready and routable with no probe.

Review the CPU limits on Deployment ad (50m) and Deployment payment (20m): the replacement containers ran at exactly those limits with 92-100 percent CFS throttling while the dependencies were unreachable, so raising the limit or the startup budget would remove that starvation path.

Find and confirm the actor that issued the rollout restart of Deployments ad and payment at 2026-11-16T22:58:53Z (pod-template restartedAt annotation) using a change-history source, which is not integrated in this Run, and confirm whether the flagd adFailure on and paymentFailure 100 percent settings are intended for this environment.

gaps: No change-history integration is available, so what triggered the kubectl rollout restart of Deployments ad and payment at 2026-11-16T22:58:53Z could not be identified.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be inspected: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data both with rule_name RequestErrorRate and unfiltered (views 8829c651-475c-400f-b88b-f72ff90238b0-t0:18f48a2d-f1a0-4fc7-9b9e-0ad58693724c and 80069122-c955-4dc4-a1bf-77174568d977-t0:33482c70-98ad-4ed1-98ba-d1d14b808cd7, both status no_data), so the rule expression and whether it is still firing are unknown.

Frontend application logs returned no lines for 22:55-23:16Z (view 0c980dff-8537-4708-a1d7-6c9b2a257e15-t0:d293064a-c2e1-46a7-aa1a-082592f7119d, status no_data), so frontend-side log confirmation of the 500s is missing.

A gRPC client-duration metric query for frontend returned no_data (view 9638c4ed-bd74-4989-9eda-15fc322efdcb-t1:c34f6705-d4a4-412d-bc7f-00f0d3ea2b77), so per-status gRPC client latency and status coverage for frontend are unknown.

Jaeger trace data ends at about 23:00:01Z (data_as_of of the trace views) and those trace views are incomplete (b9218c5c-4478-4a7a-8464-b5039551d203-t0:eb4867f4-d5a9-4178-a6b6-450e3ad65bc5 is also truncated; 9a455130-786f-4ea7-8d6e-59699323018a-t1:a298b7a3-169a-4f8d-b56f-9eb54e0299a6 reports that more traces may exist), so the 23:00-23:08Z part of the incident rests on metrics only and trace-level error details for that period are unknown.

kube-state-metrics series for kube_deployment_status_replicas_available and ready, kube_pod_container_info and kube_replicaset_owner returned no_data (views db80535d-08ef-414c-9e70-28c468cada60-t0:9c543860-afdc-4d2b-be50-594f9f1cc6c1, f5234709-8199-4c42-bdad-cb81207da88b-t0:562506ff-bc16-4082-94e8-3bd86df7385c and f5234709-8199-4c42-bdad-cb81207da88b-t1:8de37d3b-d504-4356-9966-b5f9780d241c), so historical image digests and a replicas-available timeline are unknown.

The cluster-wide NetworkPolicy listing returned no objects with status no_data (view d825759f-9426-4d11-b767-d481f69fb4b8-t0:234b0b96-bc6d-4a91-b760-22b1e9f6be4b), so network policy cannot be confirmed or excluded as a fact.

Why the replacement ad and payment containers consumed CPU at their limits for several minutes after start is not observable (no container profiling or startup logs for that period); the trigger of that CPU saturation remains unknown.
The roughly 2 error spans each recorded by recommendation and fraud-detection in the window are not explained by the evidence and were not tied to this cause.
Impact on end users beyond the otel-demo load generator own 500 error spans was not verified.

Readiness of ad and payment is only shown by the pod Ready condition with no readiness probe defined, so whether those pods were truly serving before 23:07-23:09 cannot be established from readiness alone.
next_steps: Use a change-history or audit-log source to identify who or what issued the rollout restart of Deployments ad and payment at 2026-11-16T22:58:53Z.
Inspect the RequestErrorRate alerting rule and its current state in Prometheus to confirm the expression and whether it still fires.
Read the frontend container logs for 22:58-23:10Z once log retention is available, to corroborate the 500 responses and the ad and payment dial failures.
Check whether the flagd flags adFailure and paymentFailure are intentionally set to on and 100 percent in this environment and revert them if not.
Add readiness probes and review the 50m and 20m CPU limits for the ad and payment containers, then re-test a rolling restart to confirm the dependencies stay reachable.

Current state is recovered: all 21 otel-demo pods are Running with ready true and restartCount 0, including ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84; ad logs (retained fragment 23:06:49-23:08:19Z) show 'no baggage found in context' and 'Targeted ad request received for [...]' with no error lines, and payment logs (fragment 23:05:33-23:08:22Z) show repeated pairs of 'Charge request received.' and 'Transaction complete.'.

The scope of recorded error spans over 22:56:33-23:16:33Z is frontend 1759.15, frontend-proxy 885.24, checkout 69.67, recommendation 2.06, fraud-detection 2.06, and 0 for ad, payment, cart and accounting; the two roughly 2-span counts are too small to tie to this failure on the evidence available.

The flagd-config ConfigMap declares fault-injection flags with adFailure defaultVariant on (Fail ad service), paymentFailure defaultVariant 100 percent (Fail payment service charge requests n percent), and adHighCpu, adManualGc, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure all off.

hypothesis.text: The fault originates in Deployment ad: its pod template was rolled at 22:58:53Z (pod-template restartedAt annotation, ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 replaced by ad-6cb57f76d), the replacement container saturated its 50m CPU limit with 92-100 percent CFS throttling for about seven minutes, and during that period connections to the ad Service ClusterIP 100.65.180.246:8080 were refused, which produced frontend GET /api/data 500s and the RequestErrorRate alert. This is a hypothesis because the evidence cannot show the internal state of the new process, and why it burned CPU at its limit is not observable.

A second, parallel fault originated in Deployment payment: its pod template was rolled at the same instant (payment-55766d76b9 replaced by payment-9c8ffb665), the replacement container ran at its 20m CPU limit with throttling 1.0, 0.928 and 0.753 in the minutes ending 23:00-23:02, and connections to the payment Service ClusterIP 100.70.188.60:8080 were refused, producing checkout PlaceOrder errors (59.77 and 4 error spans in the minutes ending 23:01 and 23:02) and frontend POST /api/checkout 500s.

Because neither container defines a readiness probe, the replacement pods were declared Ready (ad 22:58:56Z, payment 22:58:57Z) and therefore eligible as Service endpoints about 1-2 s after container start, before the applications were accepting connections; callers were therefore routed to not-yet-listening pods and received connection refused instead of being held until the backends were ready. The Ready timestamps and the missing probes are observed; the endpoint consequence is inferred.

recommendation.text: Add a gRPC readiness probe to the ad and payment containers so that Service endpoints only include pods that are actually listening; today a 1-2 s container start makes them Ready and routable with no probe.

Review the CPU limits on Deployment ad (50m) and Deployment payment (20m): the replacement containers ran at exactly those limits with 92-100 percent CFS throttling while the dependencies were unreachable, so raising the limit or the startup budget would remove that starvation path.

Find and confirm the actor that issued the rollout restart of Deployments ad and payment at 2026-11-16T22:58:53Z (pod-template restartedAt annotation) using a change-history source, which is not integrated in this Run, and confirm whether the flagd adFailure on and paymentFailure 100 percent settings are intended for this environment.

counter_evidence.text: The flagd fault settings do not match the observed failure path: the errors are TCP-level connect connection refused against the ad and payment Service ClusterIPs, the ad and payment services recorded no error spans of their own (0 over the window) and their server-side operations received no requests at all during the burst, and the ad path was serving normally again at 23:08-23:09 while the ConfigMap still declares adFailure on; an application-level flag-declared failure would not produce connection refusals.

rejected_hypothesis.text: Rejected: pod crash, OOM, eviction or node resource pressure as the cause. Both replacement pods have restartCount 0 and empty lastState, there are no OOMKilling, Evicted or NodeNotReady events in the window, and all nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure False and DiskPressure False.

Rejected: the frontend pod itself is the origin. It has been running since 2026-11-16T22:25:10Z/22:25:11Z with restartCount 0 and no restart event, its pod was not part of the 22:58:53Z rollout (only ad and payment ReplicaSets were created and deleted), and its error spans carry the downstream connection-refused diagnostics.

Rejected: the 22:58:56Z and 22:58:57Z termination of the old pods is itself the damage. The old pods were deleted by their own controller (ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete plus Deployment ScalingReplicaSet 1 to 0 at the same moment as the new ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate) with new pod names and restartCount 0, i.e. the rollout mechanism; the lasting errors come from the replacement pods being unreachable, not from the deletion event.
